findings: On the dispatch's reading of DEC-75/76 (not a paper defect): the dispatch paraphrases the argument as 'an elementary non-abelian group cannot occur'. That sentence is not in RamcovGX.tex (l.2378–2380 only cite Barbot). As a statement about groups alone it is false: the isometries of E^{1,2} whose linear part fixes a null vector form a non-abelian group with no loxodromic element (GX.exists_nonabelian_subgroup_noLox: a null rotation and a translation do not commute). What the 2+1 algebra gives is: no loxodromic ⇒ L(Γ) abelian ⇒ Γ metabelian (GX.isMetabelianOn_of_noLox). Under DEC-76 (s ≥ 1, so π₁(Σ∖sing) is free, and non-abelian means free of rank ≥ 2, hence not metabelian) the paper's assertion is TRUE; only the Lean route lacks the surface-group fact, so the hypothesis is carried as 'π₁(Reg M) not metabelian'.

RamcovGX.tex:2178–2182 / l.2230: Barbot's Prop 9.1 (Benoist, an external in lean-causal) holds in 2+1 with finite index 1 and no discreteness: GX.benoistNoLox_two. A subgroup of SO₀(1,2) without loxodromic element is commutative (GX.lorentz2_noLox_classification).
RamcovGX.tex:2379: Barbot's results give D(reg M~) ⊆ Ω⁺(Λ), not equality; the paper's '=' needs absolute maximality of reg M (already SCOPE D-12(b)).
questions: DEC-76: may the hypothesis be stated as 'π₁(Reg M) not metabelian' (or non-solvable), or must the surface-group fact (π₁(Σ∖sing) non-abelian ⇒ free of rank ≥ 2) be built? The latter needs the splitting Reg M ≅ Σ*×ℝ and the classification of π₁ of non-compact surfaces.

kb_proposals: 2+1 trace route: tr A > 3 ⇒ loxodromic for A ∈ SO₀(1,2) (GX.isLoxodromic_of_three_lt_trace, via det(A − l) = −(l−1)(l² − (trA−1)l + 1)); null/orthonormal frames IsNullFrame2/IsOrthoFrame2 give bases, coordinates, trace and det formulas.
